idea-plugin.name: Jupyter SQL Cell Variables
idea-plugin.description:
Use Python variables in PyCharm's Jupyter SQL cells. Write {{ name }} in a SQL cell, and when the cell runs, the value comes from the notebook's running kernel. The query still runs through PyCharm's own SQL cell support, over the data source picked in the cell, so there is no separate connection to set up in code.

Define values in a Python cell:

user_id = 42
products = ["Keyboard", "Monitor"]

and use them in a SQL cell:

SELECT * FROM orders
WHERE user_id = {{ user_id }}
  AND product IN {{ products }}

The data source receives WHERE user_id = 42 AND product IN ('Keyboard', 'Monitor').

Syntax

  • {{ expr }} becomes a SQL literal: 42, 1.5, 'O''Brien', NULL, TRUE, or an ISO date such as '2026-10-31'
  • A list, tuple, set, NumPy array or pandas Series becomes (1, 2, 3), ready for IN
  • A list of tuples becomes rows, ('web', 1), ('ios', 2), ready for VALUES
  • '%{{ name }}%' inside a string literal inserts the escaped text, without extra quotes
  • "{{ column }}" inside a quoted identifier inserts the name with " escaped as ""
  • {{ table | raw }} inserts str(value) unchanged, for table or column names
  • Any Python expression works, for example {{ cfg["start"] }} or {{ ids[:10] }}

Features

  • Values are read when the cell runs, so Run All sees what the cells above just produced
  • The SQL editor accepts placeholders, with no syntax errors
  • A missing variable or an unsupported value shows a short error in the cell output, and the query is not sent
  • SQL cells without placeholders behave exactly as before

Requirements

  • PyCharm 2026.2 with Jupyter SQL cells (Database Tools and SQL enabled)
  • A Python notebook kernel

Good to know

  • Values are inserted as escaped SQL literals, not bound as driver parameters. | raw inserts text unescaped, so use it only with values you trust.
  • {{name}} is added to Settings | Database | User Parameters, so SQL consoles also treat it as a parameter. You can turn it off there.
  • The plugin hooks into internal parts of PyCharm's SQL cell support, so each PyCharm release needs a matching plugin build. If those internals change, SQL cells fall back to PyCharm's normal behaviour.

Addresses PY-92307: Jupyter SQL cells should support Python variables in the query text.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.0

  • First release: {{ expr }} and {{ expr | raw }} placeholders in Jupyter SQL cells
  • Literal conversion for numbers, strings, booleans, None, dates, decimals, collections and rows
  • Placeholders are accepted by the SQL editor without syntax errors
  • Short error messages in the cell output when a placeholder can't be evaluated
